text.p: Brazil's telecoms giant Telebras said it adjusted its 1996 results to reflect a revaluation of long-distance unit Embratel, the sale of a stake in Rio Grande do Sul state telecoms CRT and tax incentive.
The company said in a published statement that it raised its 11-month net profit by 30.164 million reais to 2.97 billion reais to reflect Embratel's revaluation.
The firm said its sale of a five-percent stake in CRT in December added 51.111 million reais to its full-year 1996 financial results.
Telebras also said an incentive related to income taxes on profit on inflation added 65.088 million reais to its annual results.
Telebras' total 1996 results, which are not due until March, were not available Monday.
In late December, the company posted a 2.43 billion reais consolidated 11-month net profit and net earnings of 2.94 billion reais.
